newsitem.title: USA: FBI identifies three more in Olympic bomb photos.
newsitem.headline: FBI identifies three more in Olympic bomb photos.

text.p: The FBI said on Wednesday investigators of the Olympic Park bombing have identified three more people photographed near the spot where the deadly pipe bomb was planted.

The enhanced frame of a videotape showed three people walking along the north side of a sound and light tower in Centennial Olympic Park shortly after midnight on July 27. One had on a "Cheesehead" hat like those worn by fans of the Green Bay Packers in Wisconsin.
The finding brought to seven the number of people identified from four photos and a composite drawing released by the FBI last month. The pictures showed nine people altogether.
The three in the videotape frame were originally misidentified as a group of Georgia men. They later turned out not to have been in the park at the right time.
"It was actually a family of four. We've talked to them and they've provided useful information," said FBI spokesman Jay Spadafore. "They're not from Georgia."

All nine people were in Centennial Olympic Park in downtown Atlanta between 12:15 a.m. and 12:45 a.m. on July 27. During those 30 minutes, investigators say, the pipe-bomb was set under a bench at the foot of the sound and light tower in a green military-style backpack.
The bomb exploded at 1:20 a.m. during a crowded outdoor concert, leaving two people dead and more than 100 wounded.
Spadafore said investigators still had not been able to identify two people.

One person, wearing what looked like a backpack, appeared only as a blurry figure in an enhanced photograph. The second person was a white man in his 20s with a goatee, who had been seen sitting on the bench after 12:30 a.m. and was shown in a composite drawing.
Federal officials have stressed that the people in the pictures were not suspects. They simply were wanted for questioning in case they had information that could lead investigators to the bomber.
